lines.say: This week, President Trump and Xi Jinping spoke by phone about trade and Taiwan.
But in 1972, a visit to Beijing changed the world's balance of power.
In February 1972, President Nixon flew to Beijing. No American president had ever set foot in Communist China.
On the day he arrived, he shook hands with Chairman Mao.
At a banquet, he raised a glass with Premier Zhou Enlai, after more than twenty years of silence between the two countries.
He and his wife Pat walked on the Great Wall.
Now the same two powers are bargaining again, and Taiwan is still on the table.
Is China a partner or a rival?
